title: An erased write through `object` or `mixed` stores an object of the wrong class in an anonymous object, and a typed read then reads the wrong object's memory.
text: With `type Narrow = {pet: Dog};`, the program `Narrow $n = {pet: new Dog()}; object $o = $n; $o->pet = new Animal(); echo $n->pet->name;` stores the `Animal` and then panics on a misaligned read in a debug build; `mixed $m = $n; $m->pet = ...` does the same. An anonymous object's class is named for its field names alone (`nvs_ir::lower::shape_class_label`), so `write_erased_property` checks its slot by tag, and `Tag::Object` answers for every class; an array's elements and a union's arms in such a slot are not checked either. A declared class's slot is checked in full (`ClassDesc::field_checks`). The shape-view half of this hole is closed: a shape value's field types are invariant in the checker (`rule:types/shape-type`, `crates/nvs-types/src/expr/assign.rs:481`). Carrying a declared type per anonymous object was declined by the user for the shape-view half, because it costs memory per object and a check per write. A fix that spends nothing per object: an erased write into an anonymous object's slot accepts an object only when its class is the slot's current value's class or a subclass of it, and an array or a union value only when the current value has the same shape, and throws otherwise, which refuses some writes the declared type would allow.
